name: Maule M-series
variants: M-7 / MX-7 (incl. tricycle MT-7 and turbine M-7-420)
summary: Family of four-to-five-seat STOL bush planes with tube-and-fabric fuselages, popular on floats and in the backcountry.

wings: Strut-braced high wing with long-span flaps
engines: Single flat-four or flat-six in a short, deep cowl
fuselage: Tube-and-fabric four-to-five-seat fuselage with large rear windows and rear cargo door
Tailwheel gear on most (some tricycle versions); often on floats
tail: Swept fin with a squared-off top and large rudder

tellTales: Fabric-covered high-wing four-seater on a tailwheel
Swept fin with a squared-off top
Short, stubby nose and large rear cabin windows

confusedWith.howToTell: The 180/185 is all-metal with a smoothly tapered rear fuselage; the Maule is fabric-covered with a square-topped swept fin.
The Super Cub is a narrow tandem two-seater with a rounded tail; the Maule is a wider four-seater with a squared-off swept fin.
The Citabria is a narrow tandem two-seater; the Maule has a wider four-seat cabin and a swept fin.
The Maule has a squared, boxier fuselage and tail; the Sedan has a rounded fabric fuselage and a curved tail.
The Maule seats four with side-by-side front seats in a boxier cabin; the Husky seats two in tandem.
A Maule's wing is braced by a lift strut and has simple flaps; the Helio Courier has a strut-free cantilever wing with slats and huge flaps, a taller fin and much taller gear.
